what: The change of PR C as it then stood (commit a71f562: the rows of the exact nets of se_e2_a with 16 lanes a slot in float32 in a force kernel of their own, the trainer's force kernel of the rows with 16 too, and the narrow blocks of se_e2_a's kernels of the tables with the sums across the warps just past every way the device keeps at once, SE_E2A_SUMS_PAST_WAVES = 1.25) against omnimd-native-gpu-eval and omnimd-native-gpu-train of a08daf6 (base, and base2 again as the control). The rules were written before any timing (rule, with its amendment after force-sums-past-rtx4090-2026-11-22.json's second decision), the decision after them (decision): the evaluation's 16 lanes and the sums failed their rules and were taken out, the trainer's 16 lanes stayed by their own, with no gain measured. The checks ran on edbe6a0 (checks) and, after the review, on a1ba76f, which adds a float32 case of the trainer with an odd number of slots and words a comment of the kernels' source more fully (checks_after_review). See SUMMARY.md, 2026-11-23.
beside_the_timings: Two processes of `find / -maxdepth 6 -type d -name cudarc-...` (left by agents of an earlier review, one core each; stopping them was not allowed in the session) ran beside the timings of force-lanes-rtx4090-2026-11-22.json and were still running at its end (2026-11-22 22:25, checked); by 2026-11-23 00:28 they were gone (checked). These timings ran without them (checked at the start of the chain and at its end).
rule: Written 2026-11-22 23:45, before any timing of PR C (branch force-exact-lanes, commit 7d1dee4 and its fixes). The timings:
prc_ab.py, 5 rounds, base = run/prev-a08daf6, new = this branch, base2 = base again (the control), held to the
P-cores with the card checked before every round; ab_small.py (the small set of #44), 3 rounds; t_ba2.py, the
trainer, 3 rounds of 3,000 steps in float32 and in float64, before = the trainer of a08daf6 (run/fl/train-new.exe,
the build of 4f6c4ed, whose sources a08daf6 kept).
Spread of a case: |base2 / base - 1| of the measure the rule names (least of the rounds).
Rule 1, the 16 lanes of the exact nets in float32. They stay if (a) the least forces stage of float32 water with the
exact nets at 1,536 and at 12,288 atoms is not slower than base beyond max(spread, 1%), and (b) no float32 case with
the exact nets (water 192, 1,536, 12,288; HAP 88 and 224 atoms; the committee of four; batches of 968 and 1,408
centers) has a least evaluation slower than base beyond max(spread, 1%). Otherwise the evaluation's exact kernel takes
8 lanes again in float32. The trainer's rows kernel goes by its own result: it keeps 16 lanes in float32 if the
se_e2_a model's best rate in float32 is not lower than before beyond max(spread, 1%), else it takes 8 again.
Rule 2, the sums just past every way (SE_E2A_SUMS_PAST_WAVES = 1.25). They stay if no case of the window (float32
with tables at 968, 1,014, 1,056 and 1,120 blocks; float64 with tables at 792, 880 and 896; float32 with the exact
nets at 968, where its way lies within the limit) has a least evaluation slower than base beyond max(spread, 1%).
Otherwise the limit goes to 1.0 (no sums for se_e2_a past every way, as before).
Rule 3, everything else (passes past the limit, water with tables at 192 to 98,304 atoms in both precisions, the
small set, float64 with the exact nets, the se_e3 model in the trainer, the trainer in float64) is expected
unchanged: a case slower than base beyond max(spread, 2%) in its least evaluation is looked into, and explained or
fixed, before the PR merges.
What the record says either way: the times and ratios of every case, the ways (force_threads, force_sums) of both
builds, the header `force blocks at once` of both.
Amended 2026-11-23 00:35, before any timing of the A/B, after run/fit/sums-2.json and its decision
(run/fit/decision-sums-past-2.txt): one limit per kernel of se_e2_a, 1.25 for the kernels of the tables and none
for the kernel of the exact nets, which takes no sums past every way in either precision, as before PR C.
1. Rule 2 is the sums of the kernels of the tables. Its window: float32 with tables at 968, 1,014, 1,056 and 1,120
blocks, float64 with tables at 792, 880 and 896; their code is that of a08daf6, so there new against base is
the sums alone. The exact nets at 968 leave the window and are a case of rule 1 only. Where rule 2 says the
limit goes to 1.0: past every way that is the same as 0 (the narrow blocks without the sums, as before PR C).
2. With no sums past every way for the exact nets, new and base take the same way in every case with the exact
nets, and the cases of rule 1 measure the lanes alone. Before any ratio of them is read, the header `force
blocks at once` and the ways recorded for each such case must be the same for base and new; a case where they
differ is reported, and rule 1 does not read it.
3. The run of the lanes alone (new with --block-sums 0), added to tools/fit/prc_chain.sh before this amendment,
is dropped: there new0 would take the way of new.
4. The trainer runs with tools/fit/t_ba3.py, t_ba2.py with the date of the run in its record.

CASES, joined by ',':
  w<atoms>[-f64][-nt]: the water se_e2_a model, float32 with tables unless -f64 (float64) / -nt (the exact nets);
  hap<k>, ens4, h169, h224 [-f64][-nt]: HAP model k of hap-iter0-pre/ens4-f32 on the 88-atom frame, the committee of
    four on it, model 0 on the 169- and on the 224-atom frame;
  b<88|169|224>x<N>[-f64][-nt]: HAP model 0 on a batch of N copies of that frame (--batch N), one pass of N frames.
Every round runs every build on every case, the builds in order and reversed every other round, each run
`--bench K --profile`: the evaluation time is the bench loop's (no marks), the forces stage the profile loop's. Records
the way of the force kernel (force_threads, force_sums) and the header `force blocks at once` per build and case. The
card is checked before every round, waiting while another program uses it. Run it held to the P-cores
(tools/pk/affine.py 0xFFFC).

of run/prc/rule-ab.txt as amended at 00:35. The verdicts as tools/fit/decide_ab.py 1 printed them are in
run/prc/decide-ab-1.txt. The card was free at the start of the chain and before every round of prc_ab.py (5 rounds)
and ab_small.py (3 rounds), 0 s waited; the trainer's rounds were not checked one by one. The two processes of `find`
ran neither at the start of the chain nor at its end.
Item 2 of the amendment: the header `force blocks at once` and the ways of base and new are the same in every case
of rule 1, so rule 1 reads them all.
Rule 1 (a), met: the least forces stage of float32 water with the exact nets took 2.32% less at 1,536 atoms (spread
0.04%) and 5.53% less at 12,288 (spread 0.00%); bound 1%.
Rule 1 (b), not met: HAP at 88 atoms, one frame (hap0-nt), took 1.34% longer in its least evaluation (152.34 to
154.39 us; spread 0.09%, bound 1%), its least forces stage 10.8% longer (15.50 to 17.17 us). The other cases came
within the bound: water at 192 atoms +0.27% (forces +7.6%), at 1,536 -0.47%, at 12,288 -0.79%; HAP at 224 atoms
+0.15% (forces +3.8%); the committee of four -1.00% (forces -8.2%); batches of 968 centers +0.58% (forces +7.5%) and
of 1,408 -0.06% (forces -1.4%). So the evaluation's kernel of the exact nets takes 8 lanes again in float32. With 8
lanes in float32 and 16 in float64 it is, instance for instance, the kernel that reads the stored rows: the
evaluation launches that one for the exact nets again, as at a08daf6, and the kernel of their own
(se_e2_a_exact_backward, with ForceKernel and its residence) goes.
Rule 1, the trainer: the best rate of the se_e2_a model in float32 was 678.2 steps a second before, 674.4 after and
677.2 before again: 0.56% lower, beyond the spread (0.15%) and within the bound of max(spread, 1%). By the rule the
trainer's force kernel of the rows keeps 16 lanes in float32. No gain was measured for it: it is kept by the rule,
not as a speedup.
Rule 2, not met: HAP at 224 atoms in 5 frames with tables in float32 (b224x5: 1,120 blocks, of which the device keeps
896 at once without the sums) took 1.97% longer in its least evaluation (527.84 to 538.25 us; spread 0.03%, bound
1%), its least forces stage 10.9% longer. The others of the window: in float32 968 blocks -1.63%, 1,014 -1.01%,
1,056 +0.55% (spread 0.51%); in float64 792 +0.15%, 880 -1.18%, 896 -0.86%. The same case in the first run of the
sums (run/fit/sums-1.json: the sums forced against the build's own way, on a08daf6) came out at +0.42% with a spread
of 1.01%; this run, with a spread of 0.03%, gives +1.97%. So the limit goes to 1.0, past every way the same as 0
(item 1 of the amendment): se_e2_a takes the narrow blocks without the sums past every way, as before PR C, and by
item 5 of the amendment of run/fit/rule-sums-past-2.txt at 00:26 the code drops the rule (angular_sums_past,
SE_E2A_SUMS_PAST_WAVES) instead of keeping a limit of 0. The limit is not fitted again to this run.
Rule 3: no case slower than base beyond max(spread, 2%). The other cases of the main run came within -0.49% and
+0.37%; the small set within -1.72% and +1.88% (water 192 x 4 with tables, whose spread was 2.78%); the trainer's
other rates within +0.02% and +0.10%. Nothing to look into.
What follows for PR C: the evaluation's code is that of a08daf6 again. Of the code, what merges is the trainer's force
kernel of the rows of se_e2_a with 16 lanes a slot in float32 (as in float64), kept by its rule with no gain measured.
The builds timed as new (run/prc/new.exe and run/prc/train-new.exe, of commit a71f562) are the candidate that was
measured, not the code that merges; the checks (the suites, ptxas, compute-sanitizer) run on the code as it merges.
Not decided here, each for a rule and a run of its own: 16 lanes for the exact nets chosen by the size of the pass
(they took 2.3% and 5.5% off the forces stage of 1,536 and 12,288 water atoms and 8.2% off that of the committee of
four, and added 3.8% to 10.8% to it in single passes of 88 to 968 centers; at the evaluation the gains came to 1% at
most); a narrower window of the sums (in float32 968 and 1,014 blocks came 1.63% and 1.01% faster, in float64 880
